name: foyer-move-to-space
description:
pressing the foyer strip's 'Move to space' button hands the little window's tab to the resident same-profile space window and closes the little window - a same-profile LIVE move (the exact WebContents, no reload), not a reopen. No space picker exists yet (the real space list isn't wired to this surface), so BrowserController::MoveLittleTabToSpace picks whichever OTHER live, non-little controller Registry() holds - here that is the one and only startup space window, same profile as the little window CreateLittleWindowForExternalLink resolved it on.

Drives the real path end to end: the handover (open_url, same as external-link-little-window.json) opens the little window, then a KEYBOARD gesture (Tab, Return) fires foyerMoveToSpace through chrome.send - not a coordinate click. A coordinate measured on frame-006-t538.4.png from a throwaway measurement scenario (deleted after use) landed on the button in one capture and on the OS's own Screen & System Audio Recording reminder HUD in the next - that HUD is a periodic system reminder ('accessed 8 times in the past 30 days'), not a one-time first-launch banner the existing 'warming up ScreenCaptureKit' step absorbs, so no fixed settle time makes a coordinate click reliable here. The foyer page has exactly one focusable element (the button - traffic lights are native, not DOM), so a single Tab reliably lands on it, sidestepping the HUD's screen region entirely. full_keyboard_access is required for Tab to stop on a <button> on macOS (settings-tab-row-keyboard-focus-ring's own finding); this is a plain top-level browser window rather than a settings sheet, so it does not carry that scenario's separate focus-layer failure.

--force-renderer-accessibility is a MEASUREMENT flag (see external-link-little-window's own note): without it no window's AX subtree can be read past the native views, so ax_window_kind would answer nothing rather than the wrong thing.

actions.note: let the browser window finish first paint
the handover, through the real openURLs Apple Event - opens a little window
the little window builds, the foyer route loads, and installFoyer's foyerReady handshake lands
two windows, the little one's strip showing the handed-over URL and the button
the little window is the newest window and should already be key, but re-assert frontmost before the keyboard gesture regardless - same reasoning other scenarios added their own re-activates for
the foyer page's only focusable element is the button - lands on it directly
activates the focused button - fires the same click event a real press would
the little window should be gone; one window left, holding both tabs

assertions.desc: THE MEASUREMENT: the little window closed after the move. Before this fix the button did nothing but log - two windows would remain.
No little window left - the 'Little window closes' rule.
The one remaining window is the space, still whole - not a crash reducing the count from a different cause.

assertions.pattern: Atrium: foyer tab moved live into same-profile space
assertions.desc: Corroboration: MoveLittleTabToSpace took the same-profile branch, not the cross-profile reopen.

assertions.label: no-space-list-stub
assertions.note: the old log-only stub's line must not appear - if it does, the click landed but ran dead code (a stale binary), not the new handoff

assertions.desc: Cmd+Q still quits after the move
